authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Petrobras's Board approved extraordinary shareholder remuneration of R$15.60 billion, equal to R$1.21035949 per share, paid as interim dividends in a single installment. Payment has not yet been made.
Petrobras entered into an agreement to acquire a 42% interest in the corn ethanol producer Neomille S.A. for a total price of R$ 2.8 billion.
After an ANP regulatory ruling on the TAG sale-agreement obligations, Petrobras recognized an expense of US$ 0.7 billion in Jan-Sep/2026 within other income and expenses.

business_model.basis: Stated: the segment headings in the 6-K table of contents and results sections. The mechanism line is inferred from the segment results text.
business_model.claim: Petrobras reports three operating segments: Exploration and Production (E&P), Refining, Transportation and Marketing (RTM), and Gas and Low Carbon Energies. It is an integrated oil and gas company, as the screener record also shows.
quotes: Exploration and Production (E&P)
Refining, Transportation and Marketing
Gas and Low Carbon Energies

business_model.basis: Stated in the 6-K consolidated results section.
business_model.claim: Revenue scale is large and rose sharply in the nine months: sales revenues were US$ 90,104 million, up 37.4% from US$ 65,587 million a year earlier.
quotes: Sales revenues were US$ 90,104 million for the period Jan-Sep/2026, a 37.4% increase (US$ 24,517 million) when compared to US$ 65,587 million for the period Jan-Sep/2025

business_model.basis: Stated: the sales revenue table in the 6-K, which gives its scale as US$ million in the heading.
business_model.claim: Most revenue comes from selling oil products in Brazil, with a large export business behind it. In the nine-month table (US$ million), domestic market oil products were 49,914, diesel at 22,342 was the largest domestic line, exports were 31,267, and crude oil exports were 24,472 of that.
quotes: Domestic market oil products | 49,914 | 39,340 | 26.9

business_model.basis: Stated: the revenue bridge and the key financial table in the 6-K.
business_model.claim: Export crude revenue is driven by both volume and price. Exported crude oil revenues rose US$ 10,802 million, split almost evenly between a US$ 5,400 million volume effect and a US$ 5,402 million price effect. Average Brent was 94.05 US$/bbl against 70.85.
quotes: a US$ 10,802 million increase in exported crude oil revenues, which derives from a US$ 5,400 million increase in sales volumes, and a US$ 5,402 million increase in the average price of crude oil exports

business_model.claim: Domestic oil product revenue also depends mostly on price: domestic market oil products revenues rose US$ 10,574 million, of which US$ 9,497 million came from higher average domestic basic oil product prices and US$ 1,077 million from volumes.
quotes: a US$ 10,574 million increase in domestic market oil products revenues, which derives from a US$ 1,077 million increase in sales volumes, and a US$ 9,497 million increase in average domestic basic oil products prices

business_model.basis: Stated in the revenue table and its footnote. That distributors are customers is inferred from the footnote.
business_model.claim: Government subsidy programs now add to revenue. The nine-month table (US$ million) shows 4,750 from the road-use diesel subsidy program and 521 from gasoline and LPG programs, both nil a year earlier. The programs compensate producers and importers whose prices to distributors are at or below set levels.
quotes: enabling partial compensation to producers and importers who prove that selling prices charged to distributors are equal to or lower than the price determined in the MPs

business_model.basis: Stated in the cost of sales table and discussion.
business_model.claim: Cost of sales is dominated by production taxes, depreciation and purchased inputs. In the nine-month table (US$ million), cost of sales was 41,580, made up of production taxes 12,182, depreciation, depletion and amortization 10,460, and raw material, products for resale, materials and third-party services 19,066. The rise was mainly driven by a US$ 4,036 million increase in production taxes.
quotes: This increase was mainly driven by a US$ 4,036 million increase in production taxes, mainly reflecting the higher average Brent crude prices

business_model.basis: Stated in the 6-K discussion of other taxes.
business_model.claim: A new export tax on crude oil and diesel adds a cost tied to export sales. It cost US$ 1,954 million and is levied at 12% on crude oil exports and 50% on diesel oil exports.
quotes: The tax is levied on crude oil exports at a 12% rate and on diesel oil exports at a 50% rate.

business_model.basis: Stated in the E&P segment section of the 6-K. The mechanism is partly inferred from the stated causes.
business_model.claim: E&P is the main profit source and rests on oil and gas output. E&P sales revenues were 57,830 and gross profit 31,408 (table in US$ million). Total production was 3,358 mboed, up 13.9%, helped by new floating production units and wells.
quotes: Production of crude oil, NGL and natural gas was 3,358 mboed in the period Jan-Sep/2026, representing an increase of 13.9% compared to Jan-Sep/2025

business_model.basis: Stated in the RTM section; the mechanism is paraphrased from it.
business_model.claim: RTM earns a margin by refining and selling fuels. Its gross profit was 17,330 against 4,033 a year earlier (table in US$ million). The 6-K attributes the rise mainly to higher international crack spreads, with refinery utilization at 99%.
quotes: This increase mainly reflected higher international crack spreads, particularly for diesel and jet fuel

business_model.claim: Gas and Low Carbon Energies is a small contributor. Sales revenues were 7,165, gross profit 3,250 and operating income only 95 (table in US$ million). Gross profit rose on energy capacity reserve auction contracts and higher gas margins.
quotes: primarily due to the commencement of energy capacity reserve auction contracts starting in August 2025

business_model.basis: Stated in the capex section; the link to later production and depreciation is inferred.
business_model.claim: The business is capital-intensive and weighted to oil and gas production. Nine-month capital expenditures were 16,830 (table in US$ million), of which E&P took 14,153, or 84.1%.
quotes: our Capital Expenditures were primarily directed toward investment projects which Management believes are most profitable, relating to oil and gas production

business_model.basis: Stated in the capital management note and the liquidity table.
business_model.claim: Operating cash flow funds the business, and the 6-K shows what it is used for. Net cash from operations was 32,675 and free cash flow 18,132 (table in US$ million). Lease repayments were 7,886 and dividends paid to shareholders 5,311.
quotes: Its main source of funding is cash provided by operating activities.

business_model.basis: Stated in the consolidated results introduction and the net finance discussion.
business_model.claim: Currency matters. Accounts are reported in U.S. dollars, but the functional currency is the Brazilian real. The real appreciated 5.8% in the period and produced a foreign exchange gain of 2,713 (table in US$ million), a non-operating item. Local currency appreciation also raised refining costs.
quotes: which is the functional currency of the parent company and its Brazilian subsidiaries

business_model.claim: Full-year 2025 baseline: sales revenues were 89,195 and gross profit 42,459, with net income of 19,720 (table in US$ million). Net income was helped by a foreign exchange gain of 3,558, against a loss of 11,104 in the prior year.

business_model.basis: Stated in the two 6-K releases; the link to future fuel routes is the company's own stated aim.
business_model.claim: Management is diversifying beyond oil and gas while keeping E&P as the priority. It agreed to buy a 42% stake in a corn ethanol producer for R$ 2.8 billion, and the 2027-31 plan puts US$ 83 billion in E&P implementation.
quotes: Petrobras informs that it has entered into an agreement to acquire a 42% interest in Neomille S.A., a corn ethanol producer belonging to the CerradinhoBio Group.
Investments of US$ 83 billion are planned for the E&P Implementation Portfolio

competitive_position.claim: Petrobras is a large, growing oil and gas producer. Production reached 3,358 mboed in Jan-Sep/2026, up 13.9% on the prior-year period.
quotes: Production of crude oil, NGL and natural gas was 3,358 mboed in the period Jan-Sep/2026, representing an increase of 13.9% compared to Jan-Sep/2025

competitive_position.basis: stated for the figures; the concentration reading is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Investment is concentrated in E&P, mainly pre-salt. E&P capex was US$ 14,153 million, 84.1% of company CAPEX, with US$ 7.8 billion going to Santos Basin pre-salt production.
quotes: the development of production in the pre-salt layer of the Santos Basin (US$ 7.8 billion)

competitive_position.claim: The new business plan keeps E&P as the priority, with US$ 83 billion planned for its Implementation Portfolio.
quotes: Investments of US$ 83 billion are planned for the E&P Implementation Portfolio

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item; the persistence caveat is inferred
competitive_position.claim: The refining and marketing segment gives Petrobras an integrated position. Refinery utilization was 99% against 92%, and segment gross profit was 17,330 (table in millions) against 4,033 (table in millions).
quotes: This increase mainly reflected higher international crack spreads, particularly for diesel and jet fuel

competitive_position.basis: stated for the figures; the sensitivity reading is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Earnings are sensitive to oil prices, a threat if prices fall. Adjusted EBITDA was 46,667 (table in millions) against 31,416 (table in millions) as Brent averaged 94.05 against 70.85 (US$/bbl). Management keeps a long-term price view of US$ 70/bbl.
quotes: Even so, we have maintained our long-term price view at US$ 70/bbl, with a robust scenario at US$ 50/bbl

competitive_position.claim: Production taxes take a rising share of revenue. E&P production taxes were US$ 12,176 million, up 49.6%.
quotes: production taxes amounted to US$ 12,176 million, an increase of 49.6%

competitive_position.claim: Government measures are a named threat to margins. Other taxes rose to 2,410 (table in millions) from 399 (table in millions), including a US$ 1,954 million export tax on crude oil and road-use diesel. The rates are 12% on crude and 50% on diesel.
quotes: The tax is levied on crude oil exports at a 12% rate and on diesel oil exports at a 50% rate.

competitive_position.claim: Brazilian demand supports the domestic position. Diesel sales volume rose 2.9%, helped by reduced supply from other domestic producers. Higher third-party net imports were named as an offset.
quotes: reduced supply from other domestic producers, higher economic activity and agricultural production
These effects were partially offset by the higher biodiesel content in the blend, higher net imports by third parties and higher real diesel prices.

competitive_position.claim: Refining unit cost is rising, partly because of the stronger real. Average refining cost was US$ 3.30/bbl against US$ 2.85/bbl, up 15.8%.
quotes: primarily due to inflationary effects on personnel costs related to the collective labor agreement and refinery revitalization activities

competitive_position.claim: The balance sheet is a competitive strength. Net Debt/LTM Adjusted EBITDA fell to 1.00 from 1.42, and Gross Debt of US$ 69,970 million sits under the plan ceiling.
quotes: Gross Debt was maintained lower than the maximum level of US$ 75,000 million, with convergence to the level of US$ 65,000 million defined in the 2026-2030 Business Plan

competitive_position.basis: stated for the figures; the claim-on-cash reading is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Lease liabilities are the largest part of the debt burden. Leases were 44,332 (table in millions) of Gross Debt, against finance debt of 25,638 (table in millions). Lease repayments in the 2025 cash flow statement were 9,409 (table in millions).

competitive_position.basis: stated figures; the trade-off reading is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Reinvestment is up while operating cash flow has slipped, so fewer dividends were paid. Capex on PP&E and intangibles rose to 19,521 (table in millions) in 2025 from 12,114 (table in millions) two years earlier. Operating cash flow fell to 36,047 (table in millions) from 43,212 (table in millions), and dividends paid fell to 8,114 (table in millions) from 19,670 (table in millions).

competitive_position.basis: stated figures; the cause is inferred from the finance lines
competitive_position.claim: Revenue has been shrinking while profit swings with exchange rates. Sales revenues went 102,409, 91,416, 89,195 (table in millions) over the three years shown. Net income was 24,995, 7,605, 19,720 (table in millions), and the middle year included a foreign exchange loss of 11,104 (table in millions).

competitive_position.basis: stated figures; the burden reading is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Large long-term obligations weigh on the position. Non-current decommissioning provisions were 25,563 (table in millions), provisions for legal proceedings were 3,250 (table in millions), and judicial deposits were 14,814 (table in millions).

The gas and low-carbon segment is small and weaker. Operating income was 95 (table in millions) against 125 (table in millions). A US$ 0.7 billion TAG-related expense was recognized, and the company forecasts a lower transportation tariff.
quotes: the Company forecasts a reduction in the transportation tariff, given that current conditions remain unchanged

competitive_position.claim: Petrobras is diversifying into ethanol by agreeing to buy a 42% stake in Neomille, for a total price of R$ 2.8 billion.
quotes: The total acquisition price will be R$ 2.8 billion

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 6-K Liquidity and Capital Resources section and the glossary.
financial_health.claim: Reported liquidity at 30 September was cash and cash equivalents of US$ 6,865 million and Adjusted Cash and Cash Equivalents of US$ 12,123 million. The adjusted figure was 9,200 (table in US$ million) at year-end 2025. The adjusted measure includes government bonds, bank deposit certificates and time deposits with maturities of more than three months.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, Cash and cash equivalents amounted to US$ 6,865 million and Adjusted Cash and Cash Equivalents totaled US$ 12,123 million.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 6-K consolidated debt and reconciliation sections.
financial_health.claim: Gross debt, which includes lease liabilities, was 69,970 (table in US$ million) at 30 September, almost unchanged from 69,793 at year-end 2025. Net debt fell to 57,847 from 60,593. Net Debt/LTM Adjusted EBITDA fell to 1.00 from 1.42.
quotes: Net Debt decreased by 4.5% (US$ 2,746 million), reaching US$ 57,847 million

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 6-K consolidated debt table and the liquidity table.
financial_health.claim: Lease liabilities are the larger part of gross debt: 44,332 (table in US$ million) of lease liability against 25,638 of finance debt at 30 September. Finance debt fell from 26,441 while lease liability rose from 43,352.
quotes: Gross Debt – Sum of current and non-current finance debt and lease liability, this measure is not defined under the IFRS Accounting Standards.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 6-K and the 20-F cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Cash generation was strong in the nine months to September. Net cash from operating activities was US$ 32,675 million against 25,885 (table in US$ million) a year earlier. Free Cash Flow was US$ 18,132 million against 12,948. LTM operating cash flow was 42,837, up from 36,047 for full-year 2025.
quotes: In the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, we had net cash provided by operating activities of US$ 32,675 million and positive Free Cash Flow of US$ 18,132 million.

financial_health.basis: Brent figures are in the 6-K Key Financial Information table. The planning price view comes from the 6-K presentation. The link to cash flow is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Part of the cash flow improvement is tied to higher oil prices. Average Brent was US$/bbl 94.05 against 70.85 a year earlier. Management's long-term price view is US$ 70/bbl, with a robust scenario at US$ 50/bbl.
quotes: we have maintained our long-term price view at US$ 70/bbl, with a robust scenario at US$ 50/bbl

financial_health.basis: Stated in the reconciliation table. The interpretation is inferred from the line items.
financial_health.claim: Conversion of earnings to cash is reduced by taxes and working capital. In Jan-Sep/2026, Adjusted EBITDA was 46,667 (table in US$ million) while operating cash flow was 32,675. The reconciliation shows taxes payable of (7,165), trade and other receivables of (3,901) and inventories of (2,397).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 20-F cash flow statement and the 6-K CAPEX table.
financial_health.claim: Investment needs absorb much of the cash generated. 2025 capex was 19,521 (table in US$ million), up from 14,644 in 2024, and Jan-Sep/2026 CAPEX was 16,830 against 14,006.

financial_health.basis: Current and non-current splits are from the 20-F balance sheet. Average maturity and rate are stated in the 6-K. The reading of near-term needs is inferred.
financial_health.claim: The evidence gives no maturity schedule by year, so near-term repayments can be sized only from the balance sheet. At 31 December 2025, current finance debt was 2,186 (table in millions) and current lease liability was 10,037. Non-current finance debt was 24,255 and non-current lease liability was 33,315. The 6-K gives a weighted average maturity of outstanding debt of 11.84 years and an average interest rate of 6.7% p.a.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 6-K liquidity and debt sections.
financial_health.claim: Refinancing needs are being met from operating cash flow, with some new borrowing. In Jan-Sep/2026 the company raised US$ 3,094 million of finance debt, mainly from international banks, domestic banks and export credit agencies. It repaid US$ 6,272 million, including US$ 1,886 million of bonds repurchased or redeemed. Capital-markets debt fell to 14,975 (table in US$ million) from 17,000.
quotes: Gross Debt was maintained lower than the maximum level of US$ 75,000 million, with convergence to the level of US$ 65,000 million defined in the 2026-2030 Business Plan, mainly due to debt prepayments and scheduled repayments.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 6-K releases. The effect on liquidity is inferred because no reais-to-dollar conversion is given.
financial_health.claim: Post-quarter commitments will draw on liquidity. The board approved extraordinary dividends of R$15.60 billion on 23 November, to be paid in a single installment entirely as interim dividends. Petrobras also agreed to buy a 42% interest in Neomille for R$ 2.8 billion in total, of which R$ 1.8 billion is a primary capital contribution.
quotes: approved the payment of extraordinary shareholder remuneration in the amount of R$15.60 billion
The total acquisition price will be R$ 2.8 billion, including R$ 1.8 billion in a primary capital contribution to Neomille through the subscription of new shares.

financial_health.basis: The floor is stated in the 6-K. Comparison with the 30 September balances is inferred.
financial_health.claim: The Business Plan 2027-2031 includes a minimum cash level of US$ 6 billion. Cash and cash equivalents of 6,865 (table in US$ million) at 30 September were above that level, and adjusted cash of 12,123 was well above it.
quotes: Minimum cash of US$ 6 billion

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P2 (production table and the factors it lists); the conditions for continuation are inferred from those factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Higher oil and gas output is the main volume driver. Production rose to 3,358 mboed in Jan-Sep/2026 from 2,950 mboed a year earlier, an increase of 13.9%, mainly from new and ramping FPSOs. To continue, new units must keep starting up and ramping fast enough to outrun natural field decline.
quotes: These factors were partially offset by the natural decline in production.

growth_thesis.basis: Capex figures are stated in P2; the E&P plan figure is stated in P6; the link to future production is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Heavy E&P capital spending is what sustains production growth. E&P capex was 14,153 (US$ million) in Jan-Sep/2026 against 11,894 a year earlier, up 19.0%. The 2027-2031 plan keeps E&P as the priority, with US$ 83 billion for its Implementation Portfolio. To continue, cash flow must keep funding this spending and projects must keep passing the plan's return screens.
quotes: Investments of US$ 83 billion are planned for the E&P Implementation Portfolio

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in P2 and F2; the price-dependence is inferred from P2's revenue explanation and P3's price view.
growth_thesis.claim: Higher Brent prices lifted revenue and profit in 2026. Average Brent was 94.05 US$/bbl against 70.85 a year earlier (change 32.7), and sales revenues rose 37.4% to US$ 90,104 million. For this to continue, prices must stay elevated, yet management keeps a long-term price view of US$ 70/bbl.
quotes: Even so, we have maintained our long-term price view at US$ 70/bbl

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P2; the conditions for continuation are inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Export growth is a driver. Exports were 31,267 (US$ million) in Jan-Sep/2026 against 17,952, up 74.2%, with crude oil exports at 24,472 against 13,670. To continue, export volumes and prices must hold. The export tax on crude oil is a cost against this driver.
quotes: The tax is levied on crude oil exports at a 12% rate and on diesel oil exports at a 50% rate.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures and the stated causes are in P2; the limit on further growth is inferred from flat capacity and 99% utilization.
growth_thesis.claim: Refining and marketing profit rose sharply. Segment gross profit was 17,330 (US$ million) in Jan-Sep/2026 against 4,033, and refinery utilization reached 99% against 92%. To continue, international crack spreads must stay high. Utilization has little room to rise further, since crude distillation capacity is unchanged at 1,813 mbbl/d.
quotes: This increase mainly reflected higher international crack spreads, particularly for diesel and jet fuel

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in P2; the dependence on the measures is inferred from footnote (1) of the revenue table.
growth_thesis.claim: Domestic price increases and government subsidy programs added to revenue. Domestic market oil products revenue rose by US$ 10,574 million, of which US$ 9,497 million came from higher average prices. Subsidy-program revenue was 4,750 (US$ million) for road-use diesel and 521 for gasoline and LPG. To continue, domestic prices must stay high and the provisional measures behind the subsidy programs must stay in force.
quotes: enabling partial compensation to producers and importers who prove that selling prices charged to distributors are equal to or lower than the price determined in the MPs.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures and plan limits are stated in P2; the conditions are inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Cash generation funds growth while debt falls. Net cash from operations was 32,675 (US$ million) in Jan-Sep/2026 and free cash flow was 18,132. Net Debt/LTM Adjusted EBITDA fell to 1.00 from 1.42. To continue, operating cash flow must stay strong enough to cover capex, lease repayments and dividends within the gross debt ceiling.
quotes: Gross Debt was maintained lower than the maximum level of US$ 75,000 million

growth_thesis.basis: Segment figures are stated in P2 and the acquisition in P5; the effect on future earnings is inferred and not quantified in the packet.
growth_thesis.claim: Gas, power and low-carbon expansion is a smaller driver. Gas and Low Carbon Energies gross profit rose 21.0% to 3,250 (US$ million), helped by thermal capacity contracts that began in August and September 2026. Petrobras also agreed to buy a 42% interest in Neomille S.A., a corn ethanol producer. To matter, the new contracts and the acquisition must add earnings, which has not happened yet at the operating level.
quotes: The transaction is aligned with Petrobras’ strategy of profitably diversifying its energy portfolio and gradually expanding its presence in low-carbon businesses.

material_events.claim: Petrobras's Board approved extraordinary shareholder remuneration of R$15.60 billion, equal to R$1.21035949 per share, paid as interim dividends in a single installment. Payment has not yet been made.
quotes: approved the payment of extraordinary shareholder remuneration in the amount of R$15.60 billion

material_events.basis: stated in the cited item; completion of the transaction is not stated, so it is treated as pending
material_events.claim: Petrobras entered into an agreement to acquire a 42% interest in the corn ethanol producer Neomille S.A. for a total price of R$ 2.8 billion.
quotes: The total acquisition price will be R$ 2.8 billion

material_events.claim: Petrobras recognized a US$ 1,954 million expense for an Export Tax levied on crude oil and road-use diesel exports, charged at 12% on crude oil and 50% on diesel. This was the main driver of the rise in other taxes in Jan-Sep/2026.
quotes: The tax is levied on crude oil exports at a 12% rate and on diesel oil exports at a 50% rate.

material_events.claim: After an ANP regulatory ruling on the TAG sale-agreement obligations, Petrobras recognized an expense of US$ 0.7 billion in Jan-Sep/2026 within other income and expenses.
quotes: Based on this ruling, in Jan-Sep/2026, Petrobras recognized a US$ 0.7 billion expense within other income and expenses.

material_events.claim: Petrobras published its Business Plan 2027–31, in which the E&P segment accounts for more than 70% of planned investments over 2027–2031.
quotes: The E&P segment remains a priority and accounts for more than 70% of the company’s investments during the 2027–2031 period.

risks.basis: Price figures are stated in P2. The link to geopolitical conflicts is stated in P3. The risk of a price reversal is inferred from the gap between actual Brent and the planning price.
risks.claim: The 2026 earnings step-up rests on a Brent price well above the company's own long-term planning price. Average Brent was 94.05 in Jan-Sep/2026 against 70.85 a year earlier. The company says it kept its long-term view at US$ 70/bbl.
quotes: In 2026, geopolitical conflicts shaped the external environment, resulting in higher Brent prices and record crack spreads
Even so, we have maintained our long-term price view at US$ 70/bbl, with a robust scenario at US$ 50/bbl

risks.basis: The tax rates, the expense and its deductibility are stated in P2. The risk of renewed or changed measures is inferred from their provisional nature, and the evidence gives no expiry date.
risks.claim: Government measures are taking a growing share of export profits. In Jan-Sep/2026 Petrobras booked a US$ 1,954 million expense for an Export Tax on crude oil and road-use diesel, set by Provisional Measure No. 1,340/2026. The rates are 12% on crude exports and 50% on diesel exports.
quotes: The tax is levied on crude oil exports at a 12% rate and on diesel oil exports at a 50% rate.

risks.basis: Debt, cash and dividend figures are stated in P2 and P4. The minimum cash level is stated in P6. The stress mechanism is inferred.
risks.claim: Debt and shareholder payouts are large claims on cash. Gross Debt was US$ 69,970 million at Sep 30, 2026, of which lease liability was 44,332 (table in millions). The Business Plan caps it at a maximum of US$ 75,000 million. The Board has also approved extraordinary dividends of R$15.60 billion, payable from December 2026.
quotes: Gross Debt was maintained lower than the maximum level of US$ 75,000 million, with convergence to the level of US$ 65,000 million defined in the 2026-2030 Business Plan, mainly due to debt prepayments and scheduled repayments.
approved the payment of extraordinary shareholder remuneration in the amount of R$15.60 billion

risks.basis: Stated in P2. The size of any future tariff effect on the company is not stated.
risks.claim: A regulatory ruling under the TAG sale agreement caused a US$ 0.7 billion expense in Jan-Sep/2026. The company now forecasts a lower transportation tariff for the 2026–2030 cycle.
quotes: Petrobras recognized a US$ 0.7 billion expense within other income and expenses.
the Company forecasts a reduction in the transportation tariff

risks.basis: The figures are stated in F2 and P2. The statement of functional currency is in P2. The causal link to a weaker real is inferred from the 2024 loss, which the filings in this packet do not explain.
risks.claim: Exchange-rate swings can move reported profit sharply. In 2024 foreign exchange and indexation produced a loss of (11,104) (table in millions) and net finance expense was (15,107) (table in millions). In Jan-Sep/2026 the Real x US dollar gain was 2,713 (table in millions) against 6,282 (table in millions) a year earlier.

risks.basis: The balances are stated in F1 and F3. The risk mechanism is inferred, because the legal sections were not in the packet.
risks.claim: Legal and tax contingencies are large on the balance sheet. At Dec. 31, 2025 judicial deposits were 14,814 (table in millions), up from 11,748 (table in millions), and non-current provisions for legal proceedings were 3,250 (table in millions). The 2025 cash flow shows 1,023 (table in millions) of losses on legal, administrative and arbitration proceedings.

thesis_change.basis: stated in P2 for the production figure; the link to the earlier guidance is inferred.
thesis_change.claim: Jan-Sep/2026 production was 3,358 mboed, up 13.9%, attributed to FPSO ramp-ups and start-ups, which fits the earlier 2026 production uplift. The newer items do not restate the guidance revision or the Búzios/Atapu/Sépia and rig-availability attribution.
quotes: Production of crude oil, NGL and natural gas was 3,358 mboed in the period Jan-Sep/2026, representing an increase of 13.9% compared to Jan-Sep/2025

thesis_change.basis: inferred from the absence of FPSO count or capacity figures in the readable newer text.
thesis_change.claim: The newer items confirm that two named FPSOs started production and others ramped up. They do not address the count of additional units, the capacity increase target or the 2026 nationalizations.
quotes: start of production of the FPSOs P-78 and P-79

thesis_change.claim: Jan-Sep/2026 crude oil and NGL output was 2,702 mbbl/d, and management cites higher operational efficiency and lower maintenance-stoppage losses as drivers. This is consistent with the earlier efficiency point.
quotes: higher operational efficiency and lower volume of losses due to maintenance stoppages in Campos Basin

thesis_change.claim: The newer items reaffirm capital discipline in the BP 2027-31 and report higher operational efficiency in production. Both are consistent with the conditions the earlier point listed.
quotes: capital allocation discipline and rigorous return and resilience criteria for approving capital investment projects

thesis_change.basis: stated in P2 for the actuals; guidance is absent.
thesis_change.claim: Jan-Sep/2026 CAPEX was 16,830, up 20.2%, while operating cash flow was 32,675, up 26.2% (tables in millions). This is directionally consistent with higher cash generation funding more investment. The newer readable text does not restate the 2026 Capex guidance revision.

thesis_change.basis: stated in P2 and P3; the causal link is inferred.
